Original license: MIT

CrossOS destination: app/frontend/src/controls/FileTypeListControl.tsx
Modification: structural port — the ROW SHAPE is what transfers, and it is the fourth independent use of this repository's library shape on the frontend (after ProfileListControl and the Explorer menu list). No Swift LOGIC is copied; the seven user-facing strings this destination does carry verbatim are named, with their reference lines, in the FileTypeListControl debounce-and-flush entry below. What ports: one row per file type, in the order the New menu renders, each row carrying its own toggle, extension, menu label and default filename as separate fields rather than one summary (PreferencesView.swift:75-102, FileTypeRow.swift:19-57); a "Custom Types" divider above the first row the daemon did not write; column captions in the row's field order (:124-140); a built-in that can be turned off and renamed but never deleted (FileTypeRow.swift:96-109). Three RULES port as behaviour, because each is the reason a person does not lose work: a row whose extension is invalid stays on screen, disabled, with the reason beside it, and is never dropped out from under the person editing it (PreferencesView.swift:30-34 — :30-31 is the comment recording that such a row stays visible in the UI but never reaches the store, over the validOnly filter at :32-34; FileTypeRow.swift:82-84 is the predicate, and the two things it actually gates are the toggle's .disabled at :27 and the reason it puts beside that toggle at :136 — the reference gates nothing else with it, not even the template button at :86-94); the template editor HINTS and does not gate, so an unparseable .json body is reported and still saved (TemplateEditorSheet.swift:26-41 and :50-63 for the report, and :76-83 for the save it does not gate: the button assigns the buffer whatever the hint said, and its only .disabled at :83 is an EMPTY body, never an invalid one); and a reorder writes the COMPLETE new order rather than a move, because the daemon refuses a partial list and rightly so. validateExtension's own limits (non-empty, at most 16 characters, a-z 0-9 . _ -) are what decide what "invalid" means here. CrossOS's rows, identities, validation and persistence are the daemon's (core/pkg/filetype); the reference's eight presets, its SwiftUI drag-to-reorder DropDelegate and its UserDefaults store are not ported.
Reason for modification: language and medium port — a SwiftUI settings sheet over a local store becomes a React renderer over a daemon-served schema in a webview (§3.6c). The reference's drag handle becomes a keyboard-operable move control, because a list reorderable only by mouse is not reorderable at all for a keyboard user, and the daemon's reorder verb takes an explicit id list rather than a drop. §9.11 records newfile as DIRECT REUSE for the FinderSync helpers; this entry is a frontend use of its library SHAPE, adding no copied Swift LOGIC and no new license obligation, and the seven verbatim user-facing strings it does carry are named in the entry below.

Source file: App/PreferencesView.swift:20-34 (the debounced persist and the validOnly filter at its sink), :35-37 and :111-113 (persist(), and the Done button that calls it on the way out — its .keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction) is at :115)
Original license: MIT
Original copyright: Copyright (c) 2026 Wheel Up Labs
CrossOS destination: app/frontend/src/controls/FileTypeListControl.tsx (scheduleField, the re-arm in saveField, and the unmount flush in the pending-map cleanup)
Modification: behavioural port. NO SWIFT LOGIC IS COPIED — every rule below is reimplemented, and the two RULES that transfer are described in English here rather than lifted. SEVEN user-facing strings ARE taken verbatim, and they are named now rather than denied: (1) "Extension cannot be empty", FileTypeRow.swift:157 -> FileTypeListControl.tsx:184 (extensionProblem); (2) "Extension too long (max 16 chars)", FileTypeRow.swift:158 -> :185 (extensionProblem); (3) "Allowed: a-z, 0-9, . _ -", FileTypeRow.swift:159 -> :186 (extensionProblem); (4) "Not valid JSON yet — you can still save.", TemplateEditorSheet.swift:33 -> :240 (templateHint); (5) "Tip: shell scripts usually start with a shebang, e.g. #!/bin/sh", TemplateEditorSheet.swift:37 -> :244 (templateHint); (6) "The contents of every new file created with this type.", TemplateEditorSheet.swift:46 -> :232 (templateHint); (7) the same sentence with the interpolated variable renamed to this port's own parameter — "The contents of every new .\(extLabel) file created with this type.", TemplateEditorSheet.swift:47 -> FileTypeListControl.tsx:233 (templateHint). The first six are byte-identical string literals; the seventh differs only in the name of the variable inside its interpolation. All seven are a person-facing MESSAGE, not behaviour: the check that decides to show (3), the JSON parse that decides to show (4) and the shebang test that decides to show (5) are each rewritten in TypeScript, and the wording travels so a person who has met one build does not have to learn a second to read the other. The two RULES transfer, and the reference records its own reason for the first: "Persist off a debounce, not per keystroke: every edit used to JSON-encode the full list into UserDefaults synchronously from the row's onChange." Two keystroke-driven writes to one row collapse into one, and the write that lands carries the LAST keystroke rather than racing four versions of the same word. The interval is the reference's own — PreferencesView.swift:24 reads `.debounce(for: .milliseconds(300), scheduler: RunLoop.main)` — and 300ms is what ships. Two differences, both forced by the verb rather than chosen. The reference debounces the WHOLE list because it persists the whole list; here SET_FILE_TYPE is a validated read-modify-write of ONE existing row, so the debounce is per row. The re-arm when a write is already in flight has no reference: the debounce makes the window reachable, and dropping the edit there would lose the word a person was in the middle of typing. The SECOND rule is the reference's leave-path: it does not close its settings sheet with a write in flight, because Done is `vm.persist(); dismiss()` (PreferencesView.swift:111-113) over a persist() that writes the list (PreferencesView.swift:35-37). This port's debounce opened the same window and ended it the other way — the pending timer was cleared and its word DROPPED, so a menu label typed and a page left inside 300ms was a label the daemon never heard of, with no refusal to point at. The pending entries are now fired rather than cancelled, and a failure among them is announced, because the reference's persist() is a silent assignment that cannot report anything and a webview cannot copy that. HALF of that rule transfers and half does not, and what separates them is the TRIGGER, not the write. What transfers is COMMIT-ON-EXIT: an edit still inside the debounce window must reach the store when the surface is left, so that no word is dropped on the way out. What does NOT transfer is what makes the reference's Done worth pressing — it is an EXPLICIT, USER-INITIATED commit, a button with a visible label a person chooses, carrying `.keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)` (PreferencesView.swift:115), and it means something only because every other edit in that sheet saves itself. This port's flush is PASSIVE and AUTOMATIC: navigation fires it and nobody chose anything, so it is a different behaviour wearing the same job and this entry does not claim otherwise. It is also, deliberately, the only commit control here — and that is a decision rather than an omission. newfile's PreferencesView has no Save/Discard pair to port: `Button("Save")`, `Button("Discard")` and `Button("Revert")` appear nowhere in the repository's Swift, the sole commit control in the view is Done, and the only sheet Cancel belongs to a different sheet (TemplateEditorSheet.swift:74) — the repository's OTHER Cancel is an NSAlert button in the uninstall flow (UninstallHelper.swift:18, `confirm.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")`), not a control in the preferences UI. A visible Save here would be a control CrossOS derived from no source, and it would also promise a transactional boundary a 300ms auto-save does not have — a person who types a label and navigates away without touching a button has already been saved, whether a Save exists or not. The reference's sink also applies validOnly on the way to the store, the other half of its rule; this port has NO referent for that filter, and the entry records the absence rather than claiming a guard. newfile's row makes the extension an editable field (FileTypeRow.swift:118-139, the TextField at :125 and its validateAndNormalize onChange) and that is how a row becomes invalid; the CrossOS control has no extension field at all, because the daemon's setFileType treats (ext, baseName) as the row's identity and refuses a caller that changed either (core/cmd/crossos/finderdata.go, handleSetFileType: "A caller that changed the extension would be creating a different preset"). That constraint covers BOTH halves of the pair, and they are handled differently rather than one being waved through under the other. The extension is a plain non-issue — no row served here carries one to edit, so no row can be invalid, and a shell-side filter would be a second opinion on a question the daemon does not let anyone ask. The guard that IS load-bearing is the one extensionProblem puts on the toggle, and it is why such a row would stay visible and dark rather than vanish if the extension ever became editable. The base name is NOT a non-issue, because the daemon serves a value for it and the reference's row has a field for it: it is shown, it is readOnly, and the reason is on screen beside it. It was once neither — an enabled input on the same debounced save as the menu label, which reported a save the daemon could not accept, because the row it named no longer existed. The write path is now typed to carry 'displayName' alone, so a write to baseName is not a branch nobody took but one that cannot be written.
Reason for modification: language and medium port — a Combine sink over RunLoop.main becomes a timer in a React renderer, and the two must be settled on unmount rather than torn down with the view, which is the port's flush. A schedule sheet becomes a page over a daemon-served schema in a webview (§3.6c), so the reference's sheet-level Done has no place to live; the COMMIT half of its job does, and the unmount flush is that half — fired by navigation rather than by a person pressing Done, which is the half that does not transfer, and the reason this entry claims a rule and not a control. §9.11 records newfile as DIRECT REUSE for the FinderSync helpers and grades this repository's file-type surface under §9.10 as host-app UI whose LOGIC is not copied; the seven user-facing strings named in the Modification above are MIT text carried inside this attribution block, so they add no new license obligation, while this entry names the two intervals and the leave-path it took as behaviour.
CrossOS license: MIT
